verses.1: And Ahithophel said to Abishalom, “Choose, please, twelve thousand men. I will then come and pursue David all night long.”
verses.2: And I would come upon him. He would suffer and wring his hands in pain. I would comfort him, along with all the people who were with him. And I would take the king away by myself.
verses.3: And I will make all the people listen to you again. When that man you seek returns, then all the people will be at peace.
verses.4: And it was proclaimed in the eyes of Abshalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
verses.5: And Abshalom said, “Please call upon Hushai the Arkhyite as well.” And his voice was heard.
verses.6: And Hushai went to Absalom. Absalom said to him, “These words were spoken by Ahithophel. If you really say so, then he did speak the truth.”
verses.7: And Hushai said to Abshalom, “It’s not a good advice that Ahithophel gave at this time.”
verses.8: And Hushai said, “You know your father and his people. They are all wicked people who hate God. Your father is a warrior who will never rest until he has defeated those people.”
verses.9: Now, he was lying in one of the pits or in one of those places. At first, he was thrown into them. Then he heard a noise, and he said, “There must be an epidemic among those who follow Abshalom.”
verses.10: And he was also a son of a king, whose heart was like that of a lion. He knew everything about all of Israel. He knew that your father was a king, and that his sons were also kings.
verses.11: For I have commanded that they should gather together. All of Israel will come to you, from Dan to Beer Sheva. There will be many ships on the sea, and your faces will be among them.
verses.12: And we came to him in one of the places where he was located. We lay down on it, just as when rain falls on the land; nothing can be done about it. And among all the people who were there with him, none could do anything either.
verses.13: And if they gather in a city, and all of Israel is brought there, then they will carry the goods to that city. They will carry them along until they reach the river. But there will be no king there at all.
verses.14: And Abshalom said, “May it be good for all the people of Israel. Let us follow the advice of Achitophel. But Jehovah commanded that we should follow Achitophel’s bad advice. So, Jehovah brought evil upon Abshalom.”
verses.15: And Hushai said to Zadok and to the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised. This is what he has suggested for Absalom and for the elders of Israel. This is what I have also advised.”
verses.16: And now, send them quickly and tell David, “Do not stay here during the night in the coastal areas. Also, get away from here, so that he will not be captured by the king and by all the people who are with him.”
verses.17: And Yehonatan and Ahimelech stood at the foot of the mountain. Then the family went ahead and told them that they would go and report to King David that they were unable to enter the city.
verses.18: And a young man saw them. He reported it to Abshalom. Both of them rushed away quickly and went into the house of Ishbosheth, where there was a well in the courtyard. They entered there.
verses.19: And the woman took the pot and placed it on the surface of the river. She spread a mat over it, but nothing happened.
verses.20: And the servants of Abshalom went to the woman who was in need. They said, “Where are Ahimaaz and Yehonatan?” The woman replied, “They have left me. They went away from the pool.” But they couldn’t find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.21: And after they left, they went up from the river. They went ahead and told King David. They said to him, “Come quickly and cross the river, for Ahab is about to order you to do something terrible.”
verses.22: And David and all the people with him crossed the Jordan River. They did this until morning. No one who did not cross the Jordan River was left behind.
verses.23: And Ahithophel saw that his plan had not succeeded. So he broke the ropes, went back to his house in the city, and ordered that he be hanged and died. Then he was buried alongside his father’s body.
verses.24: And David came from Bethlehem. Abshalom crossed the Jordan River, along with all of Israel’s people.
verses.25: And Amashah was placed under Joab’s command over the army. Amashah was the son of Ish, and his name was Yitro the Israelite. He came to Abigail, who was the daughter of Nahash, and she was the sister of Zeruya. She was the wife of Joab.
verses.26: And Israel and Abshalom dwelt in the land of Gilad.
verses.27: And it happened that David entered Mahanaim, and Shobi ben Nahash came from among the sons of Israel. He was recognized as a man of great importance by all the people. And Gilad also came from among the leaders of Israel.
verses.28: Linen, ropes, and all kinds of fabric; also threads, yarns, and other materials used for weaving.
verses.29: And sheep, lambs, and calves were given to David and to the people who were with him. For the people said, “We are hungry and exhausted from the journey.”
